BURHAN:v3p121/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p121/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p121/r3.claim: Moses' reply to Pharaoh implicitly adds that Pharaoh did not enslave Moses himself: the reproach was for enslaving the Israelites.
BURHAN:v3p121/r3.anchor: نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:22/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:22/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:22/r1.claim: Pharaoh calls it a favor that he rescued and raised Moses as a baby and spared him when Israelite boys were being killed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:22/r1.anchor: bulunca alıp yetiştirmesi, özellikle onu diğer erkek çocuklar gibi öldürtmemesi idi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:22/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:22/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:22/r2.claim: Moses implies this was no genuine favor but a consequence of Pharaoh's enslavement and oppression: without the persecution and killing of boys, his mother would not have set him adrift or placed him in Pharaoh's hands.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:22/r2.anchor: eğer Firavun İsrâiloğulları’na baskı uygulamasa, özellikle erkek çocukları öldürtmeye kalkışmasaydı Mûsâ’nın annesi onu nehre bırakmak durumunda kalmayacak, Mûsâ da Firavun’un eline düşmeyecekti.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r8.claim: Moses answers Pharaoh's claimed favor from 26:18–19: raising him does not entitle Pharaoh to enslave the Israelites or silence Moses' protest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p409/r8.anchor: this no doubt is a favour but it does not mean that Pharaoh has the right to enslave all the Israelites

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r1.claim: Moses says Pharaoh's upbringing was only outwardly a favor; in truth Pharaoh's subjugation of Israel and killing its sons caused Moses to be brought up in Pharaoh's house.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r1.anchor: تعبيدك بني إسرائيل وقصدك إياهم بذبح أبنائهم فإن السبب في وقوعى عندك وحصولى في تربيتك

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r2.claim: Had Pharaoh not oppressed Israel and killed its sons, Moses's mother would have raised him instead of casting him into the river; Pharaoh cannot claim credit for the result of his own abuse.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r2.anchor: لو لم يفعل فرعون ذلك أي قهر بني إسرائيل وذبح أبنائهم لتكفلت أم موسى بتربيته ولما قذفته في اليم حتى يصل إلى فرعون

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r3.claim: Grammatically, تلك is the subject, نعمة its predicate, تمنها علي an adjective, and أن عبدت the predicate of an omitted subject meaning Pharaoh's enslavement of Moses's people.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r3.anchor: قوله تلك مبتدأ ونعمة خبرها وتمنها علي صفة وإن عبدت خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي وهي في الحقيقة تعبيد قومي

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r4.claim: The term taʿbīd means taking someone as a slave, overpowering and humiliating him; Bursevī also gives a Persian gloss for it.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r4.anchor: والتعبيد : بالفارسية (دام كردن وببند كي كرفتن) يقال عبدته إذا أخذته عبدا وقهرته وذللته

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r5.claim: Moses first answered Pharaoh's reproach as an attack on his prophethood, then addressed the alleged favor without denying its factual truth and showed its real consequence was a favor.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r5.anchor: رد موسى عليه السلام أولا ما وبخه فرعون قدحا في نبوته ثم رجع إلى ما عده عليه من النعمة ولم يصرح برده حيث كان صدقا

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r6.claim: One commentator says Pharaoh began like a vulgar commoner by recalling that he had fed and favored God's prophet; mannah is a weighty favor.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : بدأ فرعون بكلام السفلة ومن على نبي الله بما أطعمه والمنة النعمة الثقيلة

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r7.claim: Mannah can mean an actual deed of favor; properly, only God truly does this, as in the verse about God favoring believers.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r7.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون ذلك بالفعل فيقال : من فلان على فلان إذا أثقله بالنعمة وعلى ذلك قوله تعالى : {لقد من الله على المؤمنين}

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r8.claim: Mannah can also mean verbally recounting a favor, normally reprehensible except when answering ingratitude; sayings warn that such reminders destroy good deeds but can expose ungratefulness.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r8.anchor: والثاني : أن يكون ذلك بالقول وذلك مستقبح فيما بين الناس إلا عند كفران النعمة ولقبح ذلك قيل : المنة تهدم الصنيعة

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r9.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r9.claim: Al-Tirmidhī says spiritual chivalry does not consist in recalling favors to those one has helped; Pharaoh showed his lack of chivalry by doing so to Moses.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r9.anchor: قال محمد بن علي الترمذي قدس سره : ليس من الفتوة تذكار الصنائع وتعدادها على من اصطنعت إليه

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r10.claim: Humans can manifest divine gentleness in a way angels cannot, which is why the angels prostrated to humanity.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r10.anchor: ليعلم أن للإنسان استعدادا في إظهار صفة اللطف لم يكن للملك ولذلك صار الإنسان مسجودا للملك والملك ساجده

BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r11.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r11.claim: This Sufi reading makes Moses a manifestation of divine gentleness and Pharaoh a manifestation of overpowering wrath; prophetic hardship brings both to the fullness of their contrasting dispositions, a pattern repeated in every age.
BURSEVI:v6p194#3/r11.anchor: كذا في "التأويلات النجمية" وقس عليهما كل موسى وكل فرعون في كل عصر إلى قيام الساعة فإن الأشياء تتبين بالأضداد وتبلغ إلى كمالها

QIRAAT-ER:26:22:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:26:22:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:26:22:9#1/r1.claim: The variant treats the hamza-alif sequence differently in orthography, reflecting canonical approaches to foreign-origin hamza without semantic impact.
QIRAAT-ER:26:22:9#1/r1.anchor: orthographic variation with no semantic impact; reflects canonical reading traditions' different approaches to foreign-origin hamza

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p74/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p74/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p74/r1.claim: Qatadah says Moses tells Pharaoh that enslaving the Israelites is the supposed favor Pharaoh holds over him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p74/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ وتلك نعمة تمنها علي ﴾ قال يقول موسى لفرعون أتمن علي أن اتخذت أنت بني إسرائيل عبيدا

QASHANI:26:20-24/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:20-24/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:20-24/r3.claim: Pharaoh’s enslavement of Israel was oppression, not a favor: bodily nature cast Moses into the body-coffin in prime matter, while spiritual powers would have raised him otherwise.
QASHANI:26:20-24/r3.anchor: إذ لو لم تعبدهم لما ألقتني أمي الطبيعة البدنية

QASHANI:26:20-24/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:20-24/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:20-24/r8.claim: The passage depicts the veiled self as unable to know the Real, prophetic wisdom, or religious law; it resists obedience, asserts itself, and seeks to overpower revelation.
QASHANI:26:20-24/r8.anchor: وهذه المقالة إشارة إلى أن النفس المحجوبة بمعقولها لا تهتدي إلى معرفة الحق وحكمة الرسالة والشرع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r8.claim: “That favor” points back to the act implicit in Pharaoh's reminder that he raised Moses as a child.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r8.anchor: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي: وتلك إشارة إلى المصدر المفهوم من قوله: ألم نربك فينا وليدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r9.claim: The apparent sense acknowledges Pharaoh's raising as a favor, while arguing that it does not negate Moses' mission; al-Suddī and al-Ṭabarī adopt this reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r9.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا الكلام إقرار من موسى عليه السلام بالنعمة، كأنه يقول: وتربيتك لي نعمة علي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r10.speaker: السدي، والطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r10.claim: Al-Suddī and al-Ṭabarī adopt the acknowledgment reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r10.anchor: وإلى هذا التأويل ذهب السدي والطبري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r11.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r11.claim: Qatāda reads the statement as a denial: Pharaoh cannot claim kindness when he oppressed Israel and should not have killed or enslaved them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: هذا منه على جهة الإنكار عليه أن تكون نعمة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r12.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r12.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reads “that is a favor you have no right to claim,” supporting denial.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r12.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك: وتلك نعمة ما لك أن تمنها، وهذه قراءة تؤيد هذا التأويل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r13.speaker: الأخفش، والفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r13.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ posit an omitted interrogative hamza before the conjunction to make a rebuke.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r13.anchor: وقال الأخفش: والفراء: قبل الواو همزة استفهام يراد به الإنكار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r14.speaker: النحاس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r14.claim: Al-Naḥḥās rejects deleting the hamza because it is meaning-bearing; al-Farrāʾ allows omission with verbs of doubt and cites ترى زيدا منطلقا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r14.anchor: ورده النحاس بأنها لا تحذف، لأنها حرف يحدث معها معنى، إلا إن كان في الكلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r15.speaker: الأخفش الأصغر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r15.claim: Al-Akhfash al-Aṣghar dismisses the proposed omission as something borrowed from ordinary people's speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r15.anchor: وكان الأخفش الأصغر يقول: أخذه من ألفاظ العامة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r16.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r16.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says a rebuke may be phrased with or without a question: absent Pharaoh's killing of Israelite boys, Moses' parents would have raised him, so Pharaoh has no due favor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r16.anchor: وقال الضحاك: الكلام إذا خرج مخرج التبكيت يكون باستفهام وبغير استفهام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r17.speaker: وقيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r17.claim: Another view says Pharaoh's enslavement of Israel nullified the favor he claims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r17.anchor: وقيل: اتخاذك بني إسرائيل عبيدا أحبط نعمتك التي تمن بها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r18.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r18.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says Moses refuses to call it a favor: Israel's enslavement and the killing of their sons caused him to be raised by Pharaoh, who effectively boasts of enslaving them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r18.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وأبى، يعني موسى عليه السلام، أن يسمي نعمته أن لا نعمة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r19.claim: تعبيد means to subdue someone and make him a slave.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p147/r19.anchor: وتعبيدهم: تذليلهم واتخاذهم عبيدا، يقال: عبدت الرجل وأعبدته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r1.claim: تلك refers to an unspecified disgraceful trait, identified by أن عبدت; the latter is nominative as apposition, as in the verse about the destruction of those people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r1.anchor: تلك إشارة إلى خصلة شنعاء مبهمة، لا يدرى ما هي إلا بتفسيرها ومحل أن عبدت الرفع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj permits an accusative parsing: the act became a favor because Pharaoh enslaved Israel; without that, Moses' family would have kept him rather than cast him into the river.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب، المعنى أنها صارت نعمة علي، لأن عبدت بني إسرائيل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r3.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r3.claim: Al-Ḥawfī parses أن عبدت بني إسرائيل as an accusative of purpose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r3.anchor: وقال الحوفي: أن عبدت بني إسرائيل في موضع نصب مفعول من أجله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ parses the clause as a بدل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r4.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: بدل، ولما أخبر موسى فرعون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r13.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r13.claim: An unnamed poet uses عبد in a line asking why his people enslave him when they have many camels and slaves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p148/r13.anchor: علام يعبدني قومي وقد كثرت ... فيهم أباعر ما شاءوا وعبدان

QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r3.claim: Pharaoh counted sparing Moses’ life among the Israelites as a favor, but Moses rejects this: enslaving the Israelites is no kindness and gives Pharaoh no claim over him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p398/r3.anchor: هل استعبادك لبني إسرائيل يعد نعمة ؟ إن ذلك ليس بنعمة ، ولا لك فيها منة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r1.claim: تلك points to Pharaoh's rearing of Moses; تمنها means he counts it as a favor, with the present tense evoking the scene. Another derivation from المَنّ means enumerate as a favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r1.anchor: وتلك ( أي التربية المفهومة من قوله : ( ألم نربك ) الخ ( نعمة تمنها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r2.claim: عبد بني إسرائيل means Pharaoh subdued and enslaved them; the verb عبد الرجل means to take someone as a slave, as the cited poem illustrates.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r2.anchor: أي ذللتهم وأتخذتهم عبيدا يقال : عبدت الرجل وأعبدته إدا اتخذته عبدا قال الشاعر : علام يعبدني قومي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r3.claim: Grammarians offer several parses for أن عبدت: a predicate of an omitted subject, circumstantial or explanatory clause, apposition to تلك or نعمة, conjunction, apposition to تمنها's pronoun, or a phrase governed by an implied preposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r3.anchor: وأن وما بعدها في تأويل مصدر مرفوع على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف والجملة حالية أو مفسرة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r4.claim: Moses argues that Pharaoh's supposed favor was really a calamity: it arose from enslaving his people and intending to kill their sons; without that, Moses would not have been raised in Pharaoh's palace.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r4.anchor: نعمة ظاهرا وهي في الحقيقة نقمة حيث كانت بسبب اذلال قومي وقصدك إياهم بذبح أبنائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك، قتادة، الأخفش، الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r5.claim: Another interpretation makes the enslavement itself the “favor” Pharaoh claims, reading the clause as a repudiating question; al-Akhfash and al-Farraʾ posit an omitted interrogative hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r5.anchor: قراءة الضحاك وتلك نعمة مالك أن تمنها علي وإلى ذلك ذهب قتادة وكذا الأخفش والفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r6.speaker: السدي، الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r6.claim: Al-Suddi and al-Tabari take Moses to acknowledge Pharaoh's favor in rearing him, since Pharaoh enslaved others but spared and adopted him; al-Alusi says this is not persuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p69#3/r6.anchor: وإلى التأويل ذهب السدي والطبري وليس بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r1.claim: The verse shows that an unbeliever's disbelief does not erase a favor he previously granted; the contrary view is answered by distinguishing the grounds for praise and blame.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r1.anchor: فالآية ظاهرة في أن كفر الكافر لايبطل نعمته وذهب بعضهم أن الكفر يبطل النعمة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads إذا in the prior verse as a conditional answer: Pharaoh accused Moses of repaying his favor with the killing, and Moses accepts that he did so.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r2.anchor: وذهب الزمخشري إلى أن إذا في قوله تعالى فعلتها إذا جواب وجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r3.claim: Al-Kashf explains the conditional reading hypothetically: if the killing were ingratitude, Moses did it as repayment, but he denies it was ingratitude; “I was astray” is a second apology for acting before divine permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r3.anchor: وفي الكشف تحقيق ما ذكره الزمخشري أن الترتيب الذي هو معنى الشرط والجزاء حاصل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r4.claim: Al-Kashf's reading can accommodate وأنا من الضالين: Moses was off the right course in acting before divine permission, not in believing he owed Pharaoh repayment.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r4.anchor: وقوله : ( وأنا من الضالين ) على هذا كأنه اعتذار ثان أي كنت تستحق ذلك عندي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r5.claim: The most fitting way to sustain a recompense reading is to understand ضالين as bold action without concern for consequences.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r5.anchor: ولايخفى أن الأوفق بحديث الجزاء أن يكون المراد بقوله : فعلتها وأنا من الضالين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r6.claim: Al-Alusi says the conditional account is unnecessary: most interpreters make إذا simply an answer, while explaining it as a conditional reward here is strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r6.anchor: فان الصحيح الذي قال به الأكثرون أنها قد تتمحض للجواب وفي البحر أنهم حملوا ما في هذه الآية على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r7.claim: His preferred reading treats إذا as a temporal adverb detached from annexation; if that is refused, it functions only as an answer, not as filler.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r7.anchor: والأظهر عندي معنى ما آثره بعض أفاضل المحققين من أنها ظرف مقطوع عن الاضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya calls إذا a filler and then glosses it as “then”; al-Alusi says the latter works as an explanation of meaning, but not as a filler.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p70/r8.anchor: قول ابن عطية : إنها هنا صلة في الكلام ثم قوله : وكأنها بمعنى حينئذ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r5.claim: Exegetes differ over Moses’s “that is a favor”: some read it as acknowledgment and others as denial.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r5.anchor: اختلفوا في تأويلها: فحملها بعضهم على الإقرار وبعضهم على الإنكار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r6.claim: On the affirmative reading, Moses counts it as a favor that Pharaoh raised him without killing or enslaving him, unlike Israelite boys and people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r6.anchor: عدها موسى نعمة منه عليه حيث رباه، ولم يقتله كما قتل سائر غلمان بني إسرائيل، ولم يستعبده كما استعبد بني إسرائيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r7.claim: On the negative reading, “is this a favor?” is a question with the interrogative hamza omitted, as elsewhere in scripture and poetry.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r7.anchor: قال قوله: "وتلك نعمة" هو على طريق (1) الاستفهام، أي: أو تلك نعمة؟ حذف ألف الاستفهام، كقوله: "أفهم الخالدون"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r8.speaker: الشاعر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r8.claim: The poet’s line is cited as an example of the omitted interrogative hamza.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر (2) تروح من الحي أو تبتكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r9.speaker: عمر بن عبد الله بن أبي ربيعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r9.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Rabīʿa’s verses are cited as examples of the omitted interrogative hamza.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r9.anchor: قال عمر بن عبد الله بن أبي ربيعة: لم أنس يوم الرحيل وفقتها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r10.claim: Moses may be rebutting Pharaoh for boasting of his upbringing while forgetting his enslavement and mistreatment of the Israelites, whose humiliation also disgraced Moses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r10.anchor: وتنسى جنايتك على بني إسرائيل بالاستعباد والمعاملات القبيحة؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r11.claim: Another explanation says Pharaoh’s enslavement and killing of Israelite children put Moses in his care; without it, his own family would have raised him and he would not have been cast into the river.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r11.anchor: باستعبادك بني إسرائيل وقتلك أولادهم، دفعت إليك حتى ربيتني وكفلتني ولو لم تستعبدهم وتقتلهم كان لي من أهلي من يربيني ولم يلقوني في اليم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r12.claim: ʿAbadta means that Pharaoh made the Israelites into slaves; related forms also mean taking someone as a slave.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p110/r12.anchor: قوله: {عبدت} أي: اتخذتهم عبيدا، يقال: عبدت فلانا، وأعبدته، وتعبدته، واستعبدته، أي: اتخذته عبدا

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r1.claim: The upbringing Pharaoh calls a favor was outwardly so, but in fact Moses' arrival and rearing in Pharaoh's home resulted from enslaving Israel and killing their sons.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r1.anchor: أي وتلك التربية نعمة تمنها علي ظاهرا

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r2.claim: An alternative supplies a rhetorical hamza of denial: is this a favor you claim while enslaving Israel? The clause can be parsed as predicate, apposition, genitive with omitted باء, or accusative with it omitted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r2.anchor: وقيل إنه مقدر بهمزة الإنكار أي تلك نعمة تمنها علي

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r3.claim: Another view takes that as an allusion to a heinous trait, with enslavement of Israel explaining the claimed favor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r3.anchor: وقيل تلك إشارة إلى خصلة شنعاء مبهمة

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r4.claim: The singular you is used for the favor because Pharaoh alone imposed it, while Moses feared and fled from Pharaoh and his courtiers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:22-23/r4.anchor: وإنما وحد الخطاب في تمنها وجمع فيما قبله لأن المنة كانت منه وحده

BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r8.claim: Because Pharaoh combined reproach and boasting, Moses answers the reproach first as the later and more immediate point, then turns to the supposed favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r8.anchor: ولما اجتمع في كلام فرعون من وتعيير , بدأ بجوابه عن التعيير لأنه الأخير فكان أقرب , ولأنه أهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r9.claim: Moses's phrasing asks the question without an explicit particle of denial, keeping the rebuke concise and courteous.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p353/r9.anchor: فقال موبخا له مبكتا منكرا عليه غير أنه حذف حرف الإنكار إجمالا في القول وإحسانا في الخطاب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r1.claim: Moses recasts Pharaoh's supposed favor as the very enslavement of Israel, replacing the claimed favor with the injustice that cancels it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r1.anchor: جعله نفسها فقال مبدلا منها تنبيها على إحباطها , وإعلاما بأنها - بكونها نقمة - أولى منها في عدها نعمة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r2.claim: Israel descends from prophets, and Joseph had saved Egyptians' lives and freed them; Pharaoh's later enslavement and killing of sons led to Moses's arrival in his household.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r2.anchor: وهو أبناء الأنبياء , ولسلفهم يوسف عليه السلام عليكم من المنة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r3.claim: Pharaoh turns from Moses's rebuke because it exposed God's complete power and knowledge in the events of Moses's life, and shifts to the mission to mislead his people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p354/r3.anchor: فهم ما في جوابه هذا الأخير من الذم له والتعجيز , وإثبات القدرة التامة والعلم الشامل لله

DURR-FULL:v6p291/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p291/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p291/r9.claim: Mujāhid says Pharaoh's supposed favor was to conquer and exploit the Israelites.
DURR-FULL:v6p291/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {وتلك نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل} قال: قهرتهم واستعملتهم

DURR-FULL:v6p291/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p291/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p291/r10.claim: Qatāda expands Moses' reply: Pharaoh calls Israelite enslavement a favor despite their freedom, when he had actually conquered and enslaved them.
DURR-FULL:v6p291/r10.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {وتلك نعمة تمنها علي} قال: يقول موسى لفرعون: أتمن علي يا فرعون بأن اتخذت بني إسرائيل عبيدا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses rejects Pharaoh's supposed favor: Pharaoh enslaved the Israelites and calls that a favor to Moses.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق قال : ثم اقبل عليه موسى ينكر عليه ما ذكر من يده عنده فقال : وتلك نعمة تمنها علي ان عبدت بني اسرائيل

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says Moses challenges Pharaoh for claiming credit after taking free Israelites and making them slaves by force.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وتلك نعمة تمنها علي قال : يقول موسى لفرعون اتمن علي يا فرعون بان اتخذت من بني اسرائيل عبيدا وكانوا احرارا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid glosses enslaving the Israelites as subjugating them and forcing them into service.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ان عبدت بني اسرائيل فقهرتهم واستعملتهم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r4.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Pharaoh enslaved Israel by seizing their children, enslaving whom he wished and killing whom he wished; Moses was sent to make this known.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2755#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق ان عبدت بني اسرائيل اي ان اتخذتهم عبيدا تنزع ابنائهم من ايديهم ، فتسترق من شئت ، وتقتل من شئت

AKHFASH:v2p461/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p461/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p461/r2.claim: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي is treated as a question with أو understood; أن عبدت بني إسرائيل then explains it as a substitute for نعمة.
AKHFASH:v2p461/r2.anchor: وقال {وتلك نعمة تمنها علي} فيقال هذا استفهام كأنه قال "أو تلك نعمة تمنها" ثم فسر فقال {أن عبدت بني إسرائيل} وجعله بدلا من النعمة.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r4.claim: Moses returns to Pharaoh's opening boast about raising him, rejects its status as a favor, and treats the demonstrative as referring to the favor Pharaoh claimed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r4.anchor: ثم عاد إلى أول الكلام فكر على امتنانه عليه بالتربية فأبطله وأبى أن يسميه نعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r5.claim: One parsing makes أن عبدت an explanatory clause for تلك, strengthening the point while turning Pharaoh's intended boast against him, like the construction in 15:66.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r5.anchor: كان ذلك لزيادة تقرير المعنى مع ما فيه من قلب مقصود فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r6.claim: Another parsing puts أن عبدت in the accusative after an omitted preposition of cause: ‘because you enslaved the Children of Israel.’

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r7.claim: A third reading supplies an omitted interrogative hamza, making the line a question of repudiation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r7.anchor: وقيل الكلام استفهام بحذف الهمزة وهو استفهام إنكار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r8.claim: عبد means ‘subjugated’ or ‘humiliated,’ as shown by the causative form أعبد and a line cited by language authorities as lexical evidence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r9.claim: All three readings turn Pharaoh's supposed favor into a grievance: Moses was raised only because Pharaoh's persecution and infanticide drove his mother to place him in the river, where Pharaoh's wife found him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r9.anchor: أن نعمة تربيته ما كانت إلا بسبب إذلال بني إسرائيل إذ أمر فرعون باستئصال أطفال بني إسرائيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r10.claim: Showing kindness to Moses while oppressing his people does not make Pharaoh's treatment a favor or create a debt of gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p115/r10.anchor: وفيه أن الإحسان إليه مع الإساءة إلى قومه لا يزيد إحسانا ولا منة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r8.claim: Qatāda reads Moses’ reply as rejecting Pharaoh’s boast: sparing him was no favor when Pharaoh’s duty was not to kill him or oppress and enslave Israel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r8.anchor: فقال قتادة هذا منه على جهة الإنكار عليه أن تكون نعمة كأنه يقول أو يصح لك أن تعتمد على نعمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r9.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reads the verse as wa-tilka niʿmatun mā laka an tamunnahā, a reading supporting the rejection of Pharaoh’s claimed favor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r9.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك «وتلك نعمة ما لك أن تمنها» ، وهذه قراءة تؤيد هذا التأويل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r10.speaker: الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash proposes an omitted interrogative alif, meaning aw-tilka, but says this works only when paired with am, as in a cited poem.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r10.anchor: وقال الأخفش قيل ألف الاستفهام محذوفة والمعنى «أو تلك» وهذا لا يجوز إلا إذا عادلتها أم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r11.claim: The author calls al-Akhfash’s analysis forced; Moses’ statement is declarative without an interrogative alif and is sound as Qatāda explained.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r11.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا القول تكلف، قول موسى عليه السلام تقرير بغير ألف وهو صحيح كما قال قتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r12.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r12.claim: Al-Suddī and al-Ṭabarī instead read Moses as acknowledging the benefit of being raised and spared while noting that it does not invalidate his message.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228/r12.anchor: وقال السدي والطبري هذا الكلام من موسى عليه السلام على جهة الإقرار بالنعمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228#2/r1.claim: Both readings serve an argument: the first opposes Pharaoh and dismantles his claims; the second makes Moses fair and candid, giving his words greater force against an unfair opponent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p228#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: ولكل وجه ناحية من الاحتجاج فالأول ماض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r1.claim: The favor Pharaoh says he gave Moses means raising him; “enslaved the Children of Israel” means made them slaves, and the related verbs mean to take someone as a slave.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وتلك نعمة تمنها علي ﴾ يعني التربية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r2.claim: The particle أن has two parses: nominative as an appositive to “favor,” or accusative after an omitted preposition, understood as “because you enslaved” or “for your enslavement.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r2.anchor: وفي أن وجهان أحدهما أن تكون في موضع رفع على البدل من نعمة والثاني أن تكون في موضع نصب بنزع الخافض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r3.claim: Exegetes disagree whether Moses denies Pharaoh's claimed favor or acknowledges it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r3.anchor: واختلف العلماء في تفسير الآية ففسرها قوم على الإنكار وقوم على الإقرار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r4.claim: On the denial reading, al-Ḥasan says Pharaoh took and spent the Israelites' wealth while enslaving them, so Moses rejects the favor because it was their property.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r4.anchor: أحدها أن فرعون أخذ أموال بني إسرائيل واستعبدهم وأنفق على موسى منها فأبطل موسى النعمة لأنها أموال بني إسرائيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r5.speaker: المبرد والزجاج والأزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r5.claim: On the denial reading, had Pharaoh not killed Israelite sons, Moses' family would have raised him and his mother would not have cast him into the river; Pharaoh's persecution caused the supposed favor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r5.anchor: والثاني أن المعنى إنك لو كنت لا تقتل أبناء بني إسرائيل لكفلني أهلي وكانت أمي تستغني عن قذفي في اليم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r6.claim: On the denial reading, Pharaoh claims kindness toward Moses personally while forgetting his enslavement of the Children of Israel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r6.anchor: والثالث أن المعنى تمن علي باحسانك إلي خاصة وتنسى إساءتك بتعبيدك بني إسرائيل قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r7.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r7.claim: On the denial reading, Moses asks how Pharaoh can claim credit for raising him while enslaving his people; their humiliation cancels the personal favor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r7.anchor: والرابع أن المعنى كيف تمن علي بالتربية وقد استعبدت قومي ومن أهين قومه فقد ذل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r8.claim: On the affirmation reading, Moses counts being raised and spared enslavement as a favor, in contrast to Pharaoh's enslavement of Israel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r8.anchor: فأما من فسرها على الإقرار فانه قال عدها موسى نعمة حيث رباه ولم يقتله ولا استعبده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r9.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the acknowledgment means “you raised me and did not enslave me,” with the omitted phrase understood; he compares this to a spared servant calling it a favor that another was beaten while he was left alone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p120/r9.anchor: ثم تحذف وتركتني لان المعنى معروف هذا قول الفراء

MAJAZ:v2p84/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p84/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p84/r7.claim: The phrase means that Pharaoh took the Children of Israel as slaves.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137#3/r5.claim: Moses counters Pharaoh's claimed favor: raising one Israelite cannot compensate for enslaving and abusing the whole people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137#3/r5.anchor: أفِيفي إحسانك إلى رجل واحد منهم بما أسأت إلى مجموعهم؟ أي: ليس ما ذكرته شيئا بالنسبة إلى ما فعلت بهم.

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r7.claim: Taʿbīd means making a person a slave; the verb has the forms ʿabadtuhu and aʿbadtu-hu.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r7.anchor: والتعبيد: اتخاذ الإنسان عبدا، يقال: عبدته وأعبدته

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r10.claim: In “an ʿabbadta,” the accusative can remove an implied preposition, meaning by your enslaving or because you enslaved them.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r10.anchor: النصب بنزع الخافض أي: بتعبيدك أو لتعبيدك

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r11.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is nominative as an apposition to favor: “the favor of your enslaving.”
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r11.anchor: الرفع على البدل من النعمة، تقديره: وتلك نعمة تعبيدك

JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r20.claim: One reported interpretation treats Moses' response as acknowledging a favor.
JISHUMI:v7p5346#2/r20.anchor: أحدها: أنه اعتراف بالنعمة من موسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r11.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r11.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says enslaving the Israelites nullified the favor Pharaoh claimed toward Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r11.anchor: معناه أن اتخاذك بني إسرائيل عبيدا قد أحبط نعمتك التي تمن علي ، وهذا قول علي بن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r12.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ asks how oppressing the Israelites rather than Moses could count as a favor to Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r12.anchor: معناه أنك لما ظلمت بني إسرائيل ولم تظلمني , أعددت ذلك نعمة تمن بها علي ؟ قاله الفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r13.claim: Another view denies Pharaoh had a favor: Moses was raised by Israelites at Pharaoh’s order as part of enslaving them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r13.anchor: أنه لم تكن لفرعون على موسى نعمة لأن الذي رباه بنو إسرائيل بأمر فرعون لاستعباده لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r14.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Pharaoh paid for Moses’s upbringing from Israelite earnings taken through enslavement, so the money was not Pharaoh’s favor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r14.anchor: أن فرعون أنفق على موسى في تربيته من أموال بني إسرائيل التي أخذها من أكسابهم حين استعبدهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r15.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r15.claim: Abān ibn Taghlib says taʿbīd means confinement and humiliation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r15.anchor: أنه الحبس والإذلال , حكاه أبان بن تغلب

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r16.claim: Taʿbīd can mean enslavement, named for its humiliation, as with a road made trodden; the commentary cites Ṭarafa.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p166/r16.anchor: فالتعبيد الاسترقاق , سمي بذلك لما فيه من الإذلال , مأخوذ من قولهم طريق معبد , ومنه قول طرفة بن العبد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p168/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p168/r1.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p168/r1.claim: Ṭarafa’s line uses maʿbad for a road made smooth or trodden, illustrating the derivation of taʿbīd from humiliation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p168/r1.anchor: تبارى عناقا ناجيات وأتبعت … وظيفا فوق مور معبد أي طريق مذلل

MUJAHID:v2p460#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p460#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p460#2/r1.claim: Enslaving the Children of Israel means subjugating them, making them slaves, and putting them to work.
MUJAHID:v2p460#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ أن عبدت بني إسرائيل ﴾ يعني قهرتهم واستعبدتهم

MUQATIL:26:19-22/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:19-22/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:19-22/r4.claim: Moses says Pharaoh boasts of his kindness to him alone and forgets his wrongdoing: enslaving the Israelites for the Copts.
MUQATIL:26:19-22/r4.anchor: ثم قال لفرعون: { وتلك نعمة تمنها علي } يا فرعون تمن على بإحسانك إلى خاصة فيما زعمت، وتنسى إساءتك { أن عبدت } يقول: استعبدت { بني إسرائيل }

MUQATIL:26:19-22/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:19-22/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:19-22/r5.claim: Pharaoh oppressed the Israelites for 430 years, though another report gives forty years more; they were in Egypt when Jacob and his household came to Joseph.
MUQATIL:26:19-22/r5.anchor: وكان فرعون قد قهرهم أربع مائة وثلاثين سنة، ويقال: وأربعين سنة، وإنما كانت بنو إسرائيل بمصر حين أتاها يعقوب وبنوه وحشمه،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r1.claim: Moses rejects Pharaoh's supposed favor of raising him: enslaving Israel and killing its sons caused Moses to be brought to Pharaoh, while his parents would have raised him otherwise.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r1.anchor: كر على امتنانه عليه بالتربية فابطله من أصله وأبي أن تمسى نعمة لأنها نقمة حيث بين أن حقيقة أنعامه عليه تعبيد بنى اسرائيل لأن تعبيدهم وقصدهم بذبح أبنائهم هو السبب فى حصوله عنده وتربيته ولو تركهم لرباه ابواه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r2.claim: The singular forms for the claimed favor and enslavement refer to Pharaoh alone, while the plural forms for fear and flight include Pharaoh and his plotting group.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r2.anchor: وحد الضمير فى تمنها وعبدت وجمع فى منكم وخفتكم لأن الخوف والفرار لم يكونا منه وحده ولكن منه ومن ملته المؤتمرين بقتله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r3.claim: The vague demonstrative refers to a heinous quality then explained by enslavement; the clause is an appositive identifying that quality.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p182#4/r3.anchor: وتلك إشارة إلى خصلة شنعاء مبهمة لا يدرى ما هى إلا بتفسيرها ومحل ان عبدت الرفع عطف بيان لتلك

QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r18.speaker: السدي والطبري والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r18.claim: They read Moses as acknowledging the upbringing as a favor, while adding that Pharaoh’s enslavement of others does not negate Moses’ message.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r18.anchor: هذا الكلام من موسى عليه السلام على جهة الإقرار بالنعمة

QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r19.speaker: قتادة وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r19.claim: They take Moses to deny the alleged favor: Pharaoh enslaved and killed his people, so raising Moses was no favor he should claim.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r19.anchor: وقيل: هو من موسى عليه السلام على جهة الإنكار

QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r20.speaker: الأخفش والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r20.claim: They supply an omitted interrogative alif, reading ‘Is that a favor?’; al-Nahhas and others reject deleting the alif unless أم occurs.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r20.anchor: وقيل: فيه تقدير استفهام أي أو تلك نعمة؟

QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r21.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r21.claim: He says deleting the interrogative alif is impossible because it changes the meaning, except where أم appears, as in poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:19-21/r21.anchor: قال النحاس: وهذا لا يجوز لأن ألف الاستفهام تحدث معنى

QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r1.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r1.claim: He allows omission of the interrogative alif in verbs of doubt, citing ترى زيدا منطلقا for أترى; Ali ibn Sulayman says this came from common speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r1.anchor: قاله الفراء. قال: يجوز حذف ألف الاستفهام في أفعال الشك

QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r2.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r2.claim: He transmits al-Farra’s analogy to Abraham’s rhetorical ‘This is my lord’ and ‘Are they the immortals?’ and poetry where the interrogative alif is omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r2.anchor: الثعلبي: قال الفراء ومن قال إنها إنكار

QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r3.speaker: الغزنوي
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r3.claim: He cites a second poem as evidence that the interrogative alif can be omitted without an explicit أم.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r3.anchor: أنشد الغزنوي شاهدا على ترك الألف

QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r4.claim: He says this poem does show deletion of the interrogative alif without أم, contrary to al-Nahhas’s claim.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r4.anchor: قلت: ففي هذا حذف ألف الاستفهام مع عدم أم خلاف قول النحاس

QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r5.claim: He reads the speech as a rebuke, with or without an explicit question: had Pharaoh not killed Israelite boys, Moses’ parents would have raised him, so Pharaoh should not claim credit.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: إن الكلام خرج مخرج التبكيت والتبكيت يكون باستفهام وبغير استفهام

QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r6.claim: Another explanation is that Pharaoh cannot boast of raising Moses while humiliating Moses’ people, since a person whose people are humiliated is himself diminished.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r7.claim: أن عبدت may be nominative as an appositive to نعمة, or accusative with the sense ‘because you enslaved the Children of Israel’; al-Farra says عبدته and أعبدته are synonymous and cites poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:22/r7.anchor: في موضع رفع على البدل من

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r11.claim: Moses’s reply answers Pharaoh’s claim that he raised him: Pharaoh took him into his care because he had enslaved Israel and killed their sons.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r11.anchor: أحدها : أنه إنما وقع في يده وفي تربيته لأنه قصد تعبيد بني إسرائيل وذبح أبنائهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r12.claim: One explanation is that Pharaoh’s later kindness is outweighed and cancelled by his earlier great oppression of Israel’s ancestors.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r12.anchor: وثانيها : أن هذا الإنعام المتأخر صار معاضا بذلك الظلم العظيم على أسلافنا

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r13.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Pharaoh enslaved the Israelites, took their wealth, and spent some of it on Moses, so the upbringing was no favor.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r13.anchor: ما قاله الحسن : إنك استعبدتهم وأخذت أموالهم ومنها أنفقت علي

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r14.claim: Another explanation is that Moses was actually raised by his mother and fellow Israelites whom Pharaoh enslaved; Pharaoh merely refrained from killing him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r14.anchor: المراد أن الذي تولى تربيتي هم الذين قد استعبدتهم فلا نعمة لك علي لأن التربية كانت من قبل أمي

RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r15.claim: A final explanation: Pharaoh claimed Israel as his slaves, and a master earns no gratitude merely by feeding and supplying a slave.
RAZI-FULL:v24p109/r15.anchor: أنك كنت تدعي أن بني إسرائيل عبيدك ولا منة للمولى على العبد في أن يطعمه

RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r1.claim: The verse shows that an unbeliever’s disbelief does not erase the favor he did; Moses rejects Pharaoh’s claim by other arguments.
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r1.anchor: في الآية دلالة على أن كفر الكافر لا يبطل نعمته على من يحسن إليه ولا يبطل منته

RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r2.claim: Some scholars say an unbeliever deserves humiliation, not thanks for kindness, since thanks entails reverence and would conflict with the humiliation due for disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r2.anchor: إذا كان كافرا لا يستحق الشكر على نعمه على الناس إنما يستحق الإهانة بكفره

RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r3.claim: Other scholars hold that disbelief does not cancel gratitude for kindness, only the reward and praise earned through faith; Razi says the verse supports this view.
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r3.anchor: لا يبطل الشكر بالكفر وإنما يبطل بالكفر الثواب والمدح الذي يستحقه على الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r4.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains the plural ‘from you’ and ‘I feared you’ as including Pharaoh and the chiefs who plotted, while the singular favor and enslavement refer to Pharaoh alone.
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r4.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) إنما جمع الضمير في { منكم } و { خفتكم } مع إفراده

RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r5.claim: ‘That’ points to an unspecified disgraceful act, and ‘that you enslaved’ is its appositional clarification; the phrase means enslaving Israel is the favor Pharaoh claims.
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r5.anchor: ( تلك ) إشارة إلى خصلة شنعاء مبهمة لا يدرى ما هي إلا بتفسيرها وهي { أن عبدت } فإن { أن عبدت } عطف بيان

RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r6.claim: Razi cites the appositional construction in God’s decree to Lot as a parallel grammatical example.
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r6.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { وقضينآ إليه ذلك الامر أن دابر هؤلآء مقطوع مصبحين }

RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r7.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj offers another syntax: ‘that’ may be accusative, meaning Pharaoh’s action became a favor only because he enslaved Israel; without it Moses’s family would have sufficed.
RAZI-FULL:v24p110/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج : ويحوز أن يكون ( أن ) في موضع نصب

STUDYQURAN:26:22/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:22/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:22/r1.claim: Mannā can mean giving, counting, or boasting of and reminding others about one’s charity; 2:264 uses the latter sense.
STUDYQURAN:26:22/r1.anchor: Recount renders mannā, which has a rich range of meaning, including the sense of giving, counting, and also preening and reminding others

STUDYQURAN:26:22/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:22/r2.speaker: Moses
STUDYQURAN:26:22/r2.claim: Moses calls Pharaoh’s supposed favor the enslavement and persecution of the Israelites, asking whether that is the blessing Pharaoh claims.
STUDYQURAN:26:22/r2.anchor: Here it refers to the so-called benefaction that Pharaoh had once bestowed upon Moses, who reminds Pharaoh that the latter enslaved and persecuted the Children of Israel

TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r1.claim: Moses means Pharaoh's raising him and leaving him unenslaved while enslaving the Israelites; the omitted “and left me” is understood from context.
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r1.anchor: فرعون إياه، يقول: وتربيتك إياي، وتركك استعبادي كما استعبدت بني إسرائيل نعمة منك تمنها علي بحق

TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r2.claim: The phrase “that you enslaved the Children of Israel” can be accusative, tied to Pharaoh's claiming the favor, or nominative, explaining what the favor was.
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r2.anchor: ولأن في قوله: {أن عبدت بني إسرائيل} [الشعراء: 22] وجهين: أحدهما النصب، لتعلق {تمنها} [الشعراء: 22] بها

TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r3.claim: The verb ʿabbada means to make people slaves; al-Ṭabarī supports this usage with a line of poetry.
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r3.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {أن عبدت بني إسرائيل} [الشعراء: 22] أن اتخذتهم عبيدا لك. يقال منه: عبدت العبيد وأعبدتهم

TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r4.claim: A poem uses the verb ʿabbadanī to mean making someone a slave, supporting al-Ṭabarī's lexical gloss.
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r4.anchor: علام يعبدني قومي وقد كثرت … فيها أباعر ما شاءوا وعبدان

TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r5.claim: Mujahid explains Pharaoh's enslaving the Israelites as conquering and employing them.
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد: " { تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل} [الشعراء: 22] قال: قهرتهم واستعملتهم "

TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Pharaoh subdued, overcame, and employed the Israelites.
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: " {تمن علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل} قال: قهرت وغلبت واستعملت بني إسرائيل "

TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r7.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddī takes the claimed favor to mean that Pharaoh raised Moses as an infant.
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r7.anchor: عن السدي: " {وتلك نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل} [الشعراء: 22] وربيتني قبل وليدا "

TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r8.claim: Another reported interpretation makes Moses ask rhetorically whether Pharaoh counts enslaving the Israelites as a favor to him.
TAB-FULL:v17p559#2/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: هذا استفهام كان من موسى لفرعون، كأنه قال: أتمن علي أن اتخذت بني إسرائيل عبيدا

TAB-FULL:v17p562/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r1.claim: Qatāda reads Moses's words as a rhetorical question: does Pharaoh claim as a favor that he made the Israelites slaves?
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: " {وتلك نعمة تمنها علي} [الشعراء: 22] قال: يقول موسى لفرعون: أتمن علي أن اتخذت أنت بني إسرائيل عبيدا "

TAB-FULL:v17p562/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r2.speaker: نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r2.claim: Some Basran grammarians treat the clause as an implicit question—“Do you claim it as a favor?”—with “that you enslaved the Israelites” appositional to “favor.”
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r2.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي، فيقال: هذا استفهام كأنه قال: أتمنها علي؟ ثم فسر فقال

TAB-FULL:v17p562/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r3.claim: Another grammarian rejects that analysis as mistaken: the interrogative hamza cannot be omitted while the clause remains a question; the particle أم is evidence of interrogation.
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r3.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية ينكر هذا القول، ويقول: هو غلط من قائله لا يجوز أن يكون همز الاستفهام يلقى وهو يطلب

TAB-FULL:v17p562/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r4.speaker: أكثرهم
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r4.claim: Most grammarians take the first clause as a statement and the second as a question, treating أم as equivalent to the interrogative hamza when it follows a clause.
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r4.anchor: وقال أكثرهم: بل الأول خبر، والثاني استفهام، وكأن «أم» إذا جاءت بعد الكلام فهي الألف

TAB-FULL:v17p562/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī also cites the objection that a question may omit its initial interrogative hamza when أم follows, illustrating the construction with a poem.
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r5.anchor: قال: وقد استقبح ومعه أم، وهي دليل على الاستفهام واستقبحوا: [البحر المتقارب] تروح من الحي أم تبتكر

TAB-FULL:v17p562/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r6.speaker: نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r6.claim: The Kufan grammarians adopt al-Ṭabarī's interpretation: Pharaoh's favor was raising Moses, while he enslaved the Israelites and left Moses unenslaved.
TAB-FULL:v17p562/r6.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة في ذلك ما قلنا. وقال: معنى الكلام: وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت وأنت من الكافرين لنعمتي

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r1.claim: One reading is sarcastic: if there was a favor, it was only that Pharaoh made Moses' people slaves.
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r1.anchor: فيه وجهان أحدهما: أنه خبر على سبيل التهكم أي: إن كان ثم نعمة فليست إلا أنك جعلت قومي عبيدا لك.

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r2.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash posits an omitted interrogative hamza, yielding a question about whether this was a favor; the poet's line illustrates the omission.
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r2.anchor:
وهذا مذهب الأخفش، وجعل من ذلك قول الشاعر:
3509 أفرح أن أرزأ الكرام

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r3.claim: The discussion of the omitted interrogative is compared with an earlier example in al-Nisāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r3.anchor: وقد تقدم هذا مشبعا في سورة النساء عند قوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r4.claim: An ʿabadt can be nominative as an explanatory apposition to tilka, parallel to the construction at 15:66.
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r4.anchor: أحدها: أنها في محل رفع عطف بيان ل " تلك " ، كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r5.claim: An ʿabadt can instead be accusative as a purpose complement.
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r5.anchor: الثاني: أنها في محل نصب مفعولا من أجله.

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r6.claim: An ʿabadt can be an appositional substitute for niʿma.

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r7.claim: An ʿabadt can substitute for the pronominal hāʾ in tamunnuhā.
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r7.anchor: الرابع: أنها بدل من " ها " في " تمنها ".

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r8.claim: An ʿabadt can be genitive under an understood preposition bi.
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r8.anchor: الخامس: أنها مجرورة بباء مقدرة أي: بأن عبدت.

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r9.claim: An ʿabadt can be the predicate of an implicit subject, meaning it is that.
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r9.anchor: السادس: أنها خبر مبتدأ مضمر أي: هي.

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r10.claim: An ʿabadt can be accusative after an implicit verb meaning I mean.

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r11.claim: The clause tamunnuhā is an adjective describing niʿma.

SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r12.claim: Tamunnu normally takes bi; it may be omitted here, or the verb may carry the sense of mentioning.
SAMIN-DURR:26:22/r12.anchor: و " تمن " يتعدى بالباء فقيل: هي محذوفة أي: تمن بها، وقيل: ضمن " تمن " معنى تذكر.

TABATABAI:26:21-22/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r5.claim: Moses answers Pharaoh's boast that he is an ungrateful servant by denying that enslaving Israel is a favor: a dominion founded on oppression cannot make Pharaoh a benefactor.
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r5.anchor: أن هذا الذي تعده نعمة وتقرعني بكفرانها سلطة ظلم وتغلب إذ عبدت بني إسرائيل والتعبيد ظلما وتغلبا ليس من النعمة في شيء

TABATABAI:26:21-22/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r6.claim: The sentence is rhetorical and the phrase about enslaving Israel explains the alleged favor; calling it a favor would make enslavement itself a benefaction, an inverted cause-and-effect expression.
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r6.anchor: فالجملة استفهامية مسوقة للإنكار و { أن عبدت بني إسرائيل } بيان لما أشير إليه بقوله { تلك } والمحصل أن الذي تشير إليه

TABATABAI:26:21-22/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r7.claim: One interpretation says Moses admits that being raised in Pharaoh's home was a favor while denying that Pharaoh's not enslaving Moses was one, with an implied interrogative hamza.
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r7.anchor: أنه مسوق للاعتراف بأن تربيته لموسى كانت نعمة عليه وإنكار أن يكون ترك استعباده نعمة وهمزة الإنكار مقدرة

TABATABAI:26:21-22/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r8.claim: Tabataba'i rejects that interpretation because it requires an ellipsis unsupported by the wording.
TABATABAI:26:21-22/r8.anchor: هذا، وأنت ترى أن فيه تقديرا لما لا دليل عليه من جهة اللفظ ولا إشارة

TABATABAI:26:22-23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r1.claim: One reading takes Moses to deny Pharaoh’s claimed favor: raising him was no kindness because Pharaoh enslaved Moses’ people and thereby canceled the good deed.
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r1.anchor: إنكار لأصل النعمة عليه لمكان تعبيده بني إسرائيل كأنه يقول إن تربيتك لي ليست نعمة يمن بها علي لأنك عبدت قومي فأحبطت به عملك

TABATABAI:26:22-23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r2.claim: Although this reading seems closer than the preceding one, the author says it fails: enslaving Israel did not change the reality of Pharaoh’s kindness in raising Moses as an infant.
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r2.anchor: هذا الجواب غير تام معنى فإن تعبيده لبني إسرائيل لا يغير حقيقة ما له من الصنيعة عند موسى في تربيته وليدا

TABATABAI:26:22-23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r3.claim: Another reading makes Moses’ upbringing a consequence of Pharaoh’s oppression: enslavement forced his mother to cast him into the river, where Pharaoh found and raised him, so it was no favor.
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r3.anchor: هذه النعمة التي تمن بها علي من التربية إنما سببه ظلمك بني إسرائيل بتعبيدهم فاضطرت أمي لذلك أن ألقتني في اليم

TABATABAI:26:22-23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r4.claim: A further reading says Moses’ mother and other enslaved Israelites raised him, so his upbringing was not Pharaoh’s favor; the author judges this less supported by the wording.
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r4.anchor: أن الذي رباني أمي وغيرها من بني إسرائيل حيث استعبدتهم فأمرتهم فربوني فليست هذه التربية نعمة منك تمنها علي

TABATABAI:26:22-23/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r5.claim: Another interpretation treats the words as Moses’ admission that Pharaoh favored him by raising him while leaving him personally unenslaved.
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r5.anchor: ذلك اعتراف منه عليه السلام بنعمة فرعون عليه والمعنى وتلك التربية نعمة منك تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل وتركت تعبيدي

TABATABAI:26:22-23/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r6.claim: The author objects that the wording gives no evidence for the proposed addition, “and left me unenslaved.”
TABATABAI:26:22-23/r6.anchor: لا دليل على ما قدره من قوله وتركت تعبيدي

ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r2.claim: The commentators read Pharaoh’s words as a reproach, not an acknowledgment of a real favor: how could enslaving the Israelites be a blessing to Moses?
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r2.anchor: جهة الإنكار أن تكون تلك نعمة

ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r3.claim: Although phrased as a statement, the wording rebukes Pharaoh; it implies Moses said the enslavement of the Israelites was a favor because Pharaoh did not enslave him too.

ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r4.claim: عبد الرجل and أعبدته both mean to make someone a slave.
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r4.anchor: يقال: عبدت الرجل، وأعبدته، اتخذته عبدا

ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r5.claim: One parse makes أن a nominative apposition to نعمة: Pharaoh enslaved the Israelites but left Moses unenslaved.

ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r6.claim: Alternatively أن is accusative: Pharaoh’s persecution became a benefit because otherwise Moses’ family would have kept him rather than placing him in the river.
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r6.anchor: فإنما صارت نعمة بما فعلت من البلاء

ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v4p86/r7.claim: The quoted poem uses أعبدني to mean that the people made the speaker their slave.

TABRISI:26:20-25/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:20-25/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:20-25/r10.claim: One interpretation hears Moses acknowledge that Pharaoh's upbringing was a favor, while reproaching him for enslaving Israel rather than Moses; the question is implied.
TABRISI:26:20-25/r10.anchor: أن فيه اعترافا بأن تربيته له كانت نعمة منه على موسى وإنكارا للنعمة في ترك استعباده

TABRISI:26:20-25/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:20-25/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:26:20-25/r11.claim: Another interpretation denies that raising Moses was a favor, since Pharaoh enslaved Moses' people and thereby nullified any favor he claims.
TABRISI:26:20-25/r11.anchor: أنه إنكار للمنة أصلا ومعناه أتمن علي بأن ربيتني مع استعبادك قومي هذه ليست بنعمة

TABRISI:26:20-25/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:20-25/r12.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:26:20-25/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that without enslavement and killing Israelite sons, Moses' mother would not have cast him into the river; the claimed favor arose from Pharaoh's own oppression.
TABRISI:26:20-25/r12.anchor: أنك لو كنت لا تستعبد بني إسرائيل ولا تقتل أبناءهم لكانت أمي مستغنية عن قذفي في اليم

TABRISI:26:20-25/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:20-25/r13.speaker: الأزهري
TABRISI:26:20-25/r13.claim: Al-Azhari elaborates that Pharaoh's forbidden enslavement caused Moses' family to cast him into the river, so the upbringing became a favor only as a result of Pharaoh's wrongdoing.
TABRISI:26:20-25/r13.anchor: إنما صارت لك علي نعمة لما أقدمت عليه مما حظره الله عليك

TABRISI:26:20-25/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:20-25/r14.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:26:20-25/r14.claim: Another view says Pharaoh has no favor over Moses because his mother and fellow Israelites raised and protected him under Pharaoh's order to enslave them.
TABRISI:26:20-25/r14.anchor: أن الذي تولى تربيته أمه وغيرها من بني إسرائيل بأمر فرعون لما استعبدهم

THALABI:v7p161/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p161/r6.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v7p161/r6.claim: Al-Farra read Moses’ words as acknowledging a favor: Pharaoh raised him, did not kill or enslave him as he did Israel’s boys, and left him free.
THALABI:v7p161/r6.anchor: هو إقرار قال: عدها موسى نعمة منه عليه حيث رباه ولم يقتله كما قتل غلمان بني إسرائيل

THALABI:v7p161/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p161/r7.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p161/r7.claim: Mujahid read the words as a denial, phrased as a rhetorical question, rather than an acknowledgment of Pharaoh’s favor.
THALABI:v7p161/r7.anchor: ومن قال هو إنكار قال: معناه وتلك نعمة على طريق الاستفهام

THALABI:v7p161/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p161/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p161/r8.claim: One explanation of Moses’ denial is that, had Pharaoh not killed Israelite boys, Moses’ own parents would have raised him, so Pharaoh had no favor to claim.
THALABI:v7p161/r8.anchor: فقال: لو لم تقتل بني إسرائيل لرباني أبواي فأى نعمة لك علي؟

THALABI:v7p161/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p161/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p161/r9.claim: Other explanations are that Moses recalls Pharaoh’s crime against Israel, or argues that enslaving his people cancels any kindness shown to him.
THALABI:v7p161/r9.anchor: وقيل: ذكره إساءته إلى بني إسرائيل فقال: تمن علي أن تربيني وتنسى جنايتك على بني إسرائيل

THALABI:v7p161/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p161/r10.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p161/r10.claim: Al-Hasan said Pharaoh took the Israelites’ property, spent it on Moses, and made them slaves.
THALABI:v7p161/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: يقول: أخذت أموال بني إسرائيل وأنفقت منها علي واتخذتهم عبيدا

THALABI:v7p161/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p161/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p161/r11.claim: “You enslaved the Children of Israel” means that Pharaoh took them as slaves; grammatically the phrase can be accusative after an omitted preposition or nominative as an apposition to “favor.”
THALABI:v7p161/r11.anchor: أن عبدت بني إسرائيل أي اتخذتهم عبيدا، يقال: عبدته وأعبدته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r1.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit explains the verbs as making someone a slave and cites Ruʾba's “enslavement” wording; he also says taʿabbada and aʿbada can mean taking someone as a slave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r1.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: استعبده وعبده أي: أخذه عبدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r2.speaker: رؤبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r2.claim: Ruʾba's line uses taʿbīd for enslavement, as evidence for the wording.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit says taʿabbadtu fulānan means I took him as a slave, just like ʿabbadtuhu, and that taʾammat means taking a woman as a bondwoman.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r3.anchor: ويقال: تعبدت فلانا، أي: اتخذته عبدا، مثل: عبدته سواء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r4.claim: A further cited poetic line uses “you enslave me,” and another uses the form aʿbada for ʿabada; the poets are not named here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r4.anchor: قول الشاعر: تعبدني نمر بن سعد .. البيت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r5.claim: Mujahid says enslaving the Israelites means subjugating and putting them to work.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد، في قوله: {عبدت بني إسرائيل} قهرتهم واستعملتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r6.claim: Qatada paraphrases Moses as challenging Pharaoh to claim credit for making the Israelites slaves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة في هذه الآية: يقول موسى لفرعون: أتمن علي أن اتخذت بني إسرائيل عبيدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r7.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses contrasts Pharaoh's claimed favor in raising him with his enslavement of Israel, asking Pharaoh to release them with him and stop tormenting them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: تمن علي أن ربيتني فيك وليدا (¬6)، وأنت قد استعبدت بني إسرائيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi reads Moses as saying Pharaoh boasts of favor while enslaving the Israelites.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r8.anchor: تمن بها علي وتستعبد بني إسرائيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r9.claim: Maqatil says Moses acknowledges Pharaoh's alleged kindness to him personally while indicting the enslavement of the Israelites.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل: قال موسى: تمن علي إحسانك إلى خاصة فيما (¬2) زعمت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r10.claim: Al-Wahidi says these collected explanations do not resolve the verse's difficulty, then frames the main disagreement as whether Moses denies any favor from Pharaoh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r10.anchor: هذا ما ذكره المفسرون في هذه الآية. وهو لا يفتح غلقا ولا يحل مشكلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r11.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r11.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the phrase must be an incredulous question, understood as “or is that a favor?”, since Pharaoh's enslavement of Israel cannot be a favor to Moses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r11.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: لا يحتمل قوله: {وتلك نعمة} إلا أن يكون مستفهما به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r12.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r12.claim: The author of al-Naẓm supports an omitted interrogative hamza with Arabic usage and a poetic example meaning “Should I rejoice?”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r13.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r13.claim: Al-Akhfash similarly treats the clause as an incredulous question, with the phrase about enslaving Israel explaining or apposing to “favor.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r13.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره هو قول الأخفش؛ قال: هذا استفهام كأنه قال: أو تلك نعمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r14.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r14.claim: Abu al-Abbas rejects al-Akhfash's analysis: an interrogative cannot be omitted where it is required, especially when أم still signals a question; he cites the objectionable poetic usage “تروح من الحي أم تبتكر”.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p36/r14.anchor: قال أبو العباس: وهذا غلط لا يجوز أن يلقى الاستفهام، وهو يطلب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq reads Moses as denying Pharaoh's alleged favor: Pharaoh enslaved Israel, seized their children, enslaved or killed whom he wished, and thereby caused Moses to be brought to Pharaoh's house.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار في هذه الآية: أقبل موسى على فرعون ينكر عليه ما ذكر من يده عنده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the denial reading: “What favor was enslaving Israel to me?” The declarative wording rebukes Pharaoh, since his killing of Israelite sons forced Moses' mother to put him in the river.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r2.anchor: واختار الزجاج والأزهري هذا القول وشرحاه؛ قال الزجاج: المفسرون أخرجوا هذا على جهة الإنكار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r3.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r3.claim: Al-Azhari explains that if Pharaoh had not enslaved Israel, Moses' family would have raised him rather than casting him into the river; the supposed favor arose from Pharaoh's forbidden oppression.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r3.anchor: وزاد الأزهري بيانا لهذا القول؛ فقال: إن فرعون لما قال لموسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r4.claim: The argument works like telling someone who boasts of raising you that he could do so only after killing your parents: naming the cause rebuts the claimed favor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r4.anchor: ونظير هذا من الكلام أن يمنن إنسان على غيره تربيته فيقول له المخاطب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r5.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad likewise says Pharaoh raised Moses because of his oppression and attempted domination of Moses' people; grammatically, “that” begins the sentence, “a favor you claim” is its predicate, and “enslaving” explains the favor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p39/r5.anchor: وإلى هذا القول أشار (¬5) المبرد؛ فقال: التربية كانت بالسبب الذي ذكره الله من التعبيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r1.speaker: الفراء، وأبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r1.claim: Al-Farra and Abu al-Abbas accept that Moses acknowledges Pharaoh's upbringing as a favor: he raised Moses and spared him from the enslavement imposed on Israel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r1.anchor: القول الثاني: أن موسى أقر بنعمة التربية. وهو قول الفراء (¬1)، ومذهب أبي العباس (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r2.claim: Al-Farra's reading supplies an understood “and left me”: just as a spared servant may call it a favor that another was beaten, Moses contrasts his upbringing with Israel's enslavement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r2.anchor: ومثله في الكلام: أن تضرب أحد عبيدك وتترك الآخر، فيقول المتروك: هذه نعمة علي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r3.claim: Al-Farra allows أن to be nominative as apposition or accusative after an understood preposition, respectively yielding “your enslaving Israel” or “because you enslaved Israel.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r3.anchor: وقد تكون {أن} رفعا ونصبا، أما الرفع فعلى قولك: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi explains that the acceptance reading can be reconstructed with an omitted phrase: “the favor you mention, which you claim because you enslaved Israel.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r4.anchor: كأنه قال: وتلك التي (¬4) تذكر نعمة لك تمنها علي لأن عبدت بني إسرائيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi says the commentators' explanations show that the denial of Pharaoh's favor is the preferred interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p42/r5.anchor: ومذهب المفسرين: الإنكار. وما حكينا من أقوالهم يدل على الإنكار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:22-29/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:22-29/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:22-29/r1.claim: Moses acknowledges Pharaoh's favor in raising him, but says it was a favor only because Pharaoh did not enslave him as he enslaved Israel's children; “enslaved” means made into slaves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:22-29/r1.anchor: هي نعمة إذ ربيتني ولم تستعبدني كاستعبادك بني إسرائيل. و { عبدت } معناه: اتخذت عبيدا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r5.claim: Moses's reply refers to Pharaoh's boast about raising him and denies that this was a favor when Pharaoh had enslaved Israel.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r5.anchor: ثم قال: {وتلك نعمة تمنها علي} [الشعراء: 22] لقول فرعون له: {وأنت من الكافرين} [الشعراء: 19] لنعمتنا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r6.claim: Moses argues that Pharaoh enslaved his formerly free people, took their wealth, and used their wealth to raise him, so Moses has a stronger claim to it.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r7.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r7.claim: Mujāhid explains Pharaoh's enslavement of Israel as subjugating, torturing, and exploiting them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r7.anchor: وتفسير مجاهد: {أن عبدت بني إسرائيل} [الشعراء: 22] قهرت، وعذبت، واستعملت بني إسرائيل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r8.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r8.claim: Qatāda paraphrases Moses's rebuttal: Pharaoh boasts of enslaving a free people and subjugating them.
