YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: قال موسى لفرعون: أتمن علي يا فرعون بأن اتخذت قومي عبيدا وكانوا أحرارا فقهرتهم؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r9.speaker: ابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r9.claim: Ibn Mujāhid, transmitting his father, glosses the enslavement as subjugation.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p499/r9.anchor: وقال ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: قهرتهم.

TABRISI:26:10-12/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r10.claim: The phrase may be nominative as an appositive to “favor,” or accusative as its cause: Pharaoh’s enslavement of Israel made Moses’ survival seem a favor.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r10.anchor: إن عبدت بني إسرائيل في موضع رفع لأنه بدل من نعمة تقديره وتلك نعمة تعبيدك بني إسرائيل

TABRISI:26:10-12/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r11.claim: On the causative parsing, Pharaoh’s act becomes a “favor” only ironically: without his persecution, Moses’ family would have kept and protected him instead of casting him into the river.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب بأنه مفعول له أي إنما صارت نعمة لأن عبدت بني إسرائيل

BURHAN:v2p349/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p349/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p349/r2.claim: The interrogative hamza may be omitted, as in وتلك نعمة تمنها علي; other examples are هذا ربي under one interpretation and Ibn Muḥaysin’s reading سواء عليهم ءأنذرتهم.

BURHAN:v3p212/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p212/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p212/r5.claim: Moses' phrase omits the interrogative hamza and means 'or is that a favor you hold over me?'​
BURHAN:v3p212/r5.anchor: وقوله ﴿ وتلك نعمة تمنها علي ﴾ 4 أي أو تلك نعمة

ITQAN:v3p168/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p168/r4.speaker: ابن محيصن
ITQAN:v3p168/r4.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads “whether you warned them” without the interrogative hamza; the same omission is posited in “this is my lord” and “and is that a favor?”
ITQAN:v3p168/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن محيصن / سواء عليهم أنذرتهم / وخرج عليه ﴿ هذا ربي ﴾ في المواضع الثلاثة

ITQAN:v2p402/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p402/r18.speaker: أبو القاسم
ITQAN:v2p402/r18.claim: Abu al-Qasim says ʿabbadta in the phrase about the Children of Israel means “you killed” in Nabataean.
ITQAN:v2p402/r18.anchor: عبدت قال أبو القاسم في قوله تعالى

FARRA:v2p279/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p279/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p279/r4.claim: Moses concedes that being raised was a favor, while stressing Pharaoh did not enslave him as he enslaved the Children of Israel.
FARRA:v2p279/r4.anchor: نعمة إذ ربيتني ولم تستعبدني كاستعبادك بني إسرائيل

FARRA:v2p279/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p279/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p279/r5.claim: The wording omits “and you left me alone”; that omitted contrast is clear from the example of sparing one servant while beating another.

FARRA:v2p279/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p279/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p279/r6.claim: The clause with an may be nominative as an apposition explaining the favor, or accusative as the favor Moses is reproached for.
FARRA:v2p279/r6.anchor: أما الرفع فعلى قولك وتلك نعمة تمنها علي: تعبيدك بني إسرائيل

FARRA:v2p279/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p279/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p279/r7.claim: Arabs use both ʿabada and aʿbada for enslaving; an unnamed Arab's poem uses yaʿbudunī in this sense.
FARRA:v2p279/r7.anchor: أنشدني بعض العرب: علام يعبدني قومي وقد كثرت

NAHHAS:v3p175/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r14.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v3p175/r14.claim: Al-Akhfash suggests an omitted interrogative alif, understanding the wording as a question.
NAHHAS:v3p175/r14.anchor: قال الأخفش فقيل المعنى أو تلك نعمة وحذفت ألف الاستفهام

NAHHAS:v3p175/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p175/r15.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects omission of the interrogative alif because it changes meaning; it can be dropped only in poetry when an أم is present, apart from al-Farra's allowance in expressions of doubt.
NAHHAS:v3p175/r15.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا لا يجوز لأن الألف الاستفهام تحدث معنى وحذفها محال

NAHHAS:v3p175/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r16.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p175/r16.claim: Al-Farra allows deletion of the interrogative alif in expressions of doubt, as in ترى زيدا منطلقا for أترى; Ali ibn Sulayman attributes this to colloquial speech.
NAHHAS:v3p175/r16.anchor: إلا شيئا قاله الفراء قال يجوز حذف ألف الاستفهام في أفعال الشك

NAHHAS:v3p175/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r17.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p175/r17.claim: Al-Farra reads Pharaoh's claimed favor ironically: it would be a favor only if he had not enslaved Moses while enslaving the Israelites.
NAHHAS:v3p175/r17.anchor: ومذهب الفراء في معنى وتلك نعمة تمنها علي أنه على حذف

NAHHAS:v3p175/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r18.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v3p175/r18.claim: Al-Dahhak says Moses rebukes Pharaoh for claiming as a favor something he had no right to claim.
NAHHAS:v3p175/r18.anchor: وقول الضحاك أن المعنى أنك تمن علي بما لا يجب أن تمن به

NAHHAS:v3p175/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p175/r19.claim: The rebuke may also parallel 4:79, which says that misfortune comes from oneself.
NAHHAS:v3p175/r19.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا مثل ﴿ وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك ﴾

NAHHAS:v3p175/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p175/r20.claim: A fourth analysis supplies an omitted قول; أن عبدت can be nominative as an appositive to نعمة or accusative with the causal sense because you enslaved the Israelites.
NAHHAS:v3p175/r20.anchor: وقول رابع في الآيتين جميعا أن يكون القول محذوفا إن عبدت في موضع رفع

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r5.claim: Moses answers Pharaoh's reminder of his upbringing by citing God's gift of judgment and messengership, then overturns Pharaoh's claimed favor by pointing to his enslavement of the Israelites.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r5.anchor: فأقر بذلك موسى وذكر من أمر فراره منهم ما ذكر

NASHR:v1p279/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p279/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p279/r1.claim: Three agreed blockers to large assimilation are a first tāʾ that is a pronoun, a first letter already doubled, and a first word ending in tanwin; نعمةٌ تمنها exemplifies the last.
NASHR:v1p279/r1.anchor: وموانعه المتفق عليها ثلاثة: كون الأول تاء ضمير، أو مشددا، أو منونا

NASHR:v1p279/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p279/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p279/r2.claim: Possible but disputed blockers include jazm, few letters, successive weak changes, conversion to a madd letter, and certain consonant-context features. Equal-strength letters may assimilate; assimilating a more sonorous letter into a less sonorous one is barred, while the reverse is preferred.
NASHR:v1p279/r2.anchor: والمختلف فيه: الجزم، قيل: وقلة الحروف وتوالي الإعلال ومصيره إلى حرف مد

NASHR:v1p279/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p279/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p279/r4.claim: When the required condition and cause are present and no blocker remains, identical letters assimilate by silencing the first; unlike letters first turn into the second, then assimilate without a pause or intervening vowel.
NASHR:v1p279/r4.anchor: فإن وجد الشرط والسبب وارتفع المانع جاز الإدغام
